title: Ink droplets in motion snag top prize in Nikon Small World contest
gist: Ole Bielfeldt, a 25-year-old self-taught German photographer, won the 2026 Nikon Small World photomicrography competition, beating 1,802 entries from 69 countries, with an image of inkjet ink droplets frozen mid-air. He took apart the printer so the paper moved under a stationary printhead and used a flash in a dark room as the shutter, with no pricey equipment and no AI.

insights.claim: Ole Bielfeldt, a 25-year-old German experimental photographer, won the 2026 Nikon Small World photomicrography competition with an image of inkjet printer ink droplets landing on paper. He beat 1,802 other entries from 69 countries.
insights.speaker: Jennifer Ouellette
insights.so_what: Shows Nikon using the contest for brand marketing of its microscopy business; not a market-moving event.

insights.claim: The ink droplets moved faster than the camera's shutter speed. Bielfeldt took apart the printer so the paper moved under a stationary printhead, then shot in a dark room with a flash acting as the shutter to freeze the drops mid-air, without pricey equipment.
insights.speaker: Jennifer Ouellette
insights.so_what: An example of high-end imaging results achieved with cheap DIY methods.

insights.claim: Bielfeldt taught himself photomicrography during the COVID-19 lockdown, using an old microscope from his parents' attic connected to his father's camera with a homemade tube-and-wood adaptor. He does not use AI in his images.
insights.speaker: Jennifer Ouellette
insights.so_what: A prize-winning work made without AI is a small cultural data point for authenticity in imaging.

insights.claim: Nikon Instruments spokesperson Eric Flem says the winning image shows the microscope as a creative tool as well as a scientific one, made by using a microscope objective in an unusual way.
insights.speaker: Eric Flem
insights.so_what: Nikon is positioning its microscopy brand toward creative and consumer audiences.

insights.claim: Nikon's Small World competition, founded in 1974, is in its 52nd year. A companion Small World in Motion video competition was added in 2011, and Nikon is producing a 2027 calendar featuring the 2026 winners.
insights.speaker: Jennifer Ouellette
insights.so_what: Background on a long-running brand program; low investment relevance.
